key_insight: Personalized RewardBench is a new benchmark that measures how well reward models capture and rank individual user preferences, enabling rigorous evaluation of pluralistic, human-aligned personalization for LLMs.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks evaluate general response quality but fail to test whether reward models reflect diverse individual preferences; this work fills that gap by providing datasets, protocols, and metrics for personalized alignment.
method: Curate persona-diverse evaluation sets and preference-labeled responses to represent a wide range of individual values and styles.
Define standardized evaluation protocols (e.g., pairwise preference tests, ranking accuracy, calibration per persona) for reward models across personas.
Provide analysis metrics and baselines to quantify personalization ability, consistency, and trade-offs between general quality and individual alignment.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to diagnose and improve reward models for user-specific alignment, supporting safer and more satisfying LLM interactions across diverse user populations.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → persona labeling → RM scoring → persona-specific evaluation metrics.
Heatmap or matrix: reward-model scores vs. personas showing alignment strengths and gaps.
Bar chart: baseline RM performance (accuracy, calibration) broken down by persona groups.
Annotated example dialog: two responses with persona labels and RM preference scores to illustrate failure/success cases.
paper_title: Personalized RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models with Human Aligned Personalization
paper_authors: Qiyao Ma, Dechen Gao, Rui Cai, Boqi Zhao, Hanchu Zhou
